about.title: Inglewood Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Inglewood's workforce shows up in a lot of places at once: event and hospitality crews, warehouse and delivery workers, healthcare staff, and the construction trades. When one of those jobs leaves you hurt, the first question is usually not about lawsuits. It is about paying rent and getting seen by a doctor. California's workers' compensation system is designed to cover that, and it applies regardless of who was at fault. What many injured workers in Los Angeles County do not realize is that comp is often only part of the picture. If a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be available on top of your comp benefits. Work-related driving is a real factor here. Inglewood logged 446 injury collisions and 635 injured people in 2025, with public-record volume concentrated on Prairie Avenue, Century Boulevard, Manchester Boulevard, and La Brea Avenue. LawProactive connects you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Inglewood Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Comp is usually the limit against your employer, not against everyone
items.desc: In California, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your employer no matter who was at fault. An attorney in our network can look at whether a negligent third party, such as a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver, opens a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting fast protects you, and retaliation is against the law
items.desc: You should notify your employer within 30 days of a work injury to protect your comp benefits. If your hours get cut or you are pushed out for reporting, that is illegal retaliation, and it is worth raising with an attorney.

items.title: Third-party claims run on a two-year clock
items.desc: A claim against someone other than your employer generally must be filed within two years of the injury. Getting connected early gives an attorney time to gather site records, witness accounts, and equipment details before they disappear.

items.question: I was hit while driving for work on Century Boulevard in Inglewood. Is that only a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. If another driver caused the collision, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver, which is subject to California's two-year filing deadline. An attorney can evaluate both tracks together so they do not work against each other.

items.question: My employer says I waited too long to report my injury. Am I out of options?
items.answer: California asks you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, but a late report does not automatically end your claim in every situation. There are circumstances where the deadline is extended or the employer already had notice. It is worth having an independent attorney review the timeline before you assume the door is closed.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to connect me with an attorney in Inglewood?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You can talk through your situation without worrying about an upfront bill.
